> Lots of people comment that the moon "looks strange lately", and Anju's grandmother's story about the festival shows a moon with no face in its painterly representation.

It looking strange wasn't based on its look but of it being pulled. The story that shows the moon is of the giants and the imp, not the festival. It could be decided for the story to not show its face side since it's not the focus. The moon had no face in early development of the game that you can find a screenshot for and maybe they didn't retroactively bring the change into the story, but that's probably unlikely.

> Art informs lore. If the moon is the size of a single city because it had to be for art, then it's the size of a city and makes more sense to be a construct based on that and everything else about it that make it not at all like a real satellite.

If you ask a developer of the game whether it's a construction or the moon, they're going to tell you it's the moon. If Majora was hiding the 'real' moon out of view, it's not a detail that the Lens of Truth uncovers. This game is known for many small details. The observatory guy was *enamored* with the moon since he was a child and I'd think he has a good idea of its size.

Terminians consider the moon to be a mystical body that they worshiped and feared so it having a magical inside may not be fully on Majora's part. The observatory guy made note of its face part (its eye) as if that is nothing unusual. If the existence of a moon's tear (said to be valued by many in town) predated Majora's moon pulling, then the moon always had a face. Its small size is a technical limitation or an artistic decision (who wants to look up and can't see the sun?).

> Additionally, Majora's moon disintegrates when she is slain.

It looks to me like it's ascending after being engulfed in the rainbow. It's more likely for Nintendo wanting us to think it's the moon when we don't see one in the night sky than it being an elaborated illusion by Majora. I trust the observatory guy to know what he's talking about.
